gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-north-arab: Nippo's small letters stand almost capital-sized, with strokes that look cut from wire. And Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense band of letters whose terminals point outward.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Nippo looks drawn with a single nib, its small letters standing almost capital-sized. Noto Sans Old Persian lets its open counters breathe, so the whole pairing feels crisp and current.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Approachable despite its wire-cut precision, Nippo keeps every stroke uniform in width. Noto Sans Old Sogdian pairs wide-mouthed letters with a high x-height, staying crisp across pages of reading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Clean and technical, Nippo holds a single flat line weight through every glyph. Noto Sans Old Turkic handles the quieter work, its chunky letters and open-mouthed curves staying clear in running text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Noto Sans Oriya keeps generous gaps in its curves and lets its lowercase climb almost to capital height. Nippo's laser-cut lines, all one cutting width, supply the sharper voice up top.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-osage: Nippo draws its curves without any pinching, every stroke looking cut from wire. Noto Sans Osage fills the line with inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close up.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong reads with a high-set x-height and rounds that gap open like a cracked bangle. Nippo's ribbon-cut strokes of constant width supply the sharp, technical counterpoint.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Modern in feel, Nippo gives stems and arches identical thickness, its small letters nearly capital-sized. And Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau meets it with open-ended curves and a short step up to the capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Nippo keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, so its small, wire-cut letters read almost like capitals in a row. Noto Sans Phoenician follows, its s curves opening wide at both ends.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-runic: Nippo looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, its small letters almost capital-sized. Noto Sans Runic follows with open curves and a generous x-height.
